title: Meeting text in a test fixture; the privacy check misses meeting transcripts
description: tests/test_export.py (CHOPPED) holds lines from a real call instead of invented text. tests/test_no_personal_data.py only compares the repo with the dictation history, not with meeting/file transcripts, so it passed. Replace the lines with invented text and extend the check to transcripts. Removing it from git history is a separate decision (rewrite + GitHub purge, see dictado-gkv).
close_reason: PR #66: invented text in test_export; personal-data check covers meeting/file transcripts. Git history: Erik's decision (dictado-gkv).

title: Google Calendar sign-in: meeting names and guests (Email participants) without the secret iCal link
description: Some Google Workspace accounts have the secret iCal address turned off by the admin, so meetings get no name or guests and Email participants opens with an empty To. Add Settings > Meetings > Connect Google Calendar: a one-time sign-in in the browser (OAuth for desktop apps: loopback redirect + PKCE, read-only scope calendar.events.readonly). The background app then reads today's events like the iCal feed (title, guests' names and addresses, Meet link), picks the event of a call by time and Meet link, and Email participants on an older meeting looks up the event at its start time. The refresh token is kept on this computer only (DPAPI-encrypted on Windows). Needs an OAuth client of type Desktop app from a Google Cloud project, placed as google_client.json in the data folder.
notes: Built and merged (#101), hidden without google_client.json. The user decided not to register an app in Google Cloud for now.

title: Setup: start with English and add languages; no skipping on first run
description: The user doesn't want a wall of language chips: start with English (a fresh install), an Add a language list, and the chosen languages as removable chips. The first-run setup must not be skippable (no Skip setup, no Esc); Run setup again from Settings gets a Cancel back to Settings.
close_reason: PR #80: English first + Add a language chips; no skipping the first run.

title: Stop a meeting 10 s after its call ends, not 20 s
description: The user finds 20 s after the call app releases the mic too long. Make grace_s 10 by default, and move a saved 20 (the old default, written by every Settings save) to 10 when the config loads.
close_reason: PR #79: grace_s 10, a saved 20 reads as 10.

title: Flaky test: test_a_much_too_short_result_keeps_its_audio reads the suspect folder before the file is written
description: It waits for the output, then globs suspect/ at once; the audio is written right after, so the macos-14 runner (PR #67) saw no file. Wait for the file.
close_reason: PR #70: waits for the kept audio.

title: A meeting started by hand doesn't stop when its call ends
description: Only meetings the detector started stop at the call's end (auto_app). A meeting started by hand during a call (after Not now, or from the tray) records the call's app but keeps going until the silence backup (180 s silent + 60 s unanswered prompt, never with background sound). The user finds it takes far too long. Stop it too when the detector's end event is for the meeting's own app; a manual meeting with no call app is left alone.
close_reason: PR #68: a hand-started meeting stops when its call ends; meetwatch tests (one fails on the old code).

Show a compact chip (recording dot + timer) and expand to the full pill (label + latest live line) only while the mouse is over it. The pill stays click-through. Shared logic in meetui (short label, hover test); Windows overlay here, Mac overlay by the Mac session.

close_reason: PR #67: chip + hover on Windows, checked on the desktop; Mac in #74.

title: Mac: download progress for the mlx speech models (for the new setup)
description: The new setup (dictado-zpz) shows model download progress. models.ensure_local already reports progress(done_bytes, total_bytes|None) on Windows; on the Mac mlx_engine.ensure_mlx(repo) downloads silently via snapshot_download. Add a progress=None parameter with the same contract (monotonic, called once at the end with done == total), plus a way to ask whether a repo is already cached. Built by the Mac session, in mlx_engine.py only.
acceptance_criteria: ensure_mlx(repo, progress=cb) reports bytes while downloading and done==total at the end; already-cached repos report done==total at once; unit test with a fake downloader passes on macos-14
close_reason: PR #63 (Mac session): ensure_mlx(progress=...) and is_cached_mlx; real Mac download 0 to 481 MB, monotonic; Mac suite green.

title: Restore the clipboard after pasting; keep dictations out of clipboard history
description: Pasting a dictation overwrites whatever the user had copied, and on Windows each dictation lands in Win+V clipboard history (and cloud clipboard). Save the clipboard before the paste and restore it after; on Windows mark our clipboard writes with ExcludeClipboardContentFromMonitorProcessing / CanIncludeInClipboardHistory=0 / CanUploadToCloudClipboard=0. Mac: NSPasteboard restore (and org.nspasteboard.TransientType). Keep the existing 'no text box: keep it on the clipboard' case unchanged (then nothing is restored).
acceptance_criteria: After a dictation the previous clipboard content is back; dictations don't appear in Win+V history; the no-text-box case still leaves the text on the clipboard; both platforms
close_reason: Already built: platform/windows/deliver.py and platform/macos/deliver.py restore the previous clipboard 0.8 s after the paste and keep the transcript out of clipboard history (Windows formats / nspasteboard Transient+Concealed). Ticket made without checking.

title: New setup: full-window guided first run (languages, model download, mic, shortcut, first dictation, all set)
description: Replace the 3-step welcome card with a full-window setup. Steps: (Mac only) permissions; which languages you speak; getting your speech models ready (downloads exactly what the chosen languages need, with progress, then offline); test your microphone (level bars + mic picker); dictation shortcut (key lights up when pressed, tap or hold); try your first dictation in a mock card; all set summary (models, shortcut, mic, languages, where the app lives). Progress bar on top, heading left, live card right, Back/Continue. No survey questions, no cloud, no accounts. Shown to new installs only; Settings gets a 'Run setup again' button. Inspired by a competitor's onboarding (layout only, our own colors and font).
acceptance_criteria: New install shows the setup; existing installs don't; Run setup again works; model download shows real progress; works on Windows and Mac; smoke tests cover each step
close_reason: PR #65: full-window setup (languages, both models with download progress, mic, key, first dictation, summary; Mac permissions step), Run setup again in Settings; start page through Python (WebView2 ?page= bug). Windows: unit + smoke + the real window. Mac real run: FEATURES 'check on Mac'.

title: Clarity score + words Whisper struggled with
description: Save Whisper's word/segment confidence (avg_logprob, word probabilities) with each dictation in the local history. Engine change on both platforms (faster-whisper word_timestamps / mlx).

History gets speech_s, clarity (% words at p>=0.8), heard, unsure (p<0.5). Insights card 'How clearly you speak': score, 8-week trend, words it wasn't sure of per language. Mac: dictado-9jc.6.

title: Speech coaching: help the user speak more clearly from how they dictate
description: The user wants to improve how they speak using their dictation history. Research basis: ASR confidence correlates with intelligibility; immediate feedback reduces filler words without raising anxiety; hedges and hesitations lower perceived confidence; comprehension peaks around 130-160 wpm. Caveat: most dictation is thinking aloud to an AI, so coaching focuses on dictations to people (messages, email) and later the user's side of meetings. Everything computed locally; nothing personal ever goes in git (tests use invented text).

notes: Mac part done in #34 (mlx quick piece check + MIX_PAD_MS = 30). Windows GPU check (dictado-l2x) found turbo's quick check unreliable on short pieces; fixed with QUICK_SURE.

title: Live text on the pill while dictating + catch dictations that come back much too short
description: Show the transcript live on the pill while dictating, and catch dictations that come back far shorter than the talking (seen on long dictations; not reproduced on test audio). Live: quick greedy pass every 2 s on the last 15 s, skipped whenever the model is busy/loading; the careful pass is still what gets pasted. Diagnostics: delivered log gets speech_s + dropout_s; a result under 4 chars/s on >= 15 s keeps its audio locally in data/suspect (last 5).
notes: Reopened 2026-10-07 for the Mac session's findings: previews ran with no pill to show them (Ui always has live), and a stop tap could wait up to one preview pass.
close_reason: Merged #22 (live text) and #26 (only when the pill can show it; slow passes stretch the gap).

title: Rename Dictado -> Ecoscribe
description: Rename before going public: 'Dictado' clashes with Dictato (a paid local Mac dictation app) and several iPhone apps.
design: Phase 1 (this): everything visible -> Ogma: window/tray/pill/toasts/prompts, installer display names + Setup file names, README/FEATURES/guide, GitHub repo ErikBros/ogma (redirect). Internals unchanged: package dictado, Dictado.exe, data dirs, Run key, bundle id, MCP key. Phase 2 (after the Mac stack merges): package rename, exe name, data dir migration, installer upgrade from Dictado (old dir + Run key), MCP key, Mac bundle id (re-grant TCC), speaker add-on name.
notes: Ogma was dropped; Echotype/Echoscribe are taken in transcription; picked Ecoscribe (6 repos, none voice; GitHub user free). Phase 2 Windows half: PR #17 (package ecoscribe, Ecoscribe.exe 1.7.0, paths.migrate for Win + Mac dirs, installer upgrade from Dictado, Run key + Claude link renamed). Mac half: PR #20. Windows speaker add-on name: dictado-jtv.
close_reason: Both halves merged and installed: Windows (PR #17, 1.7.0, data/Run key/Claude link moved) and Mac (PR #20, Ecoscribe.app, TCC re-granted). Windows speaker add-on name: dictado-jtv.

title: Languages as add-ons: base English + Swedish, 'Add a language' for the rest
description: Languages as add-ons: English and Swedish built in, everything else added from an 'Add a language' picker in Settings (no download; Whisper knows ~99).
design: Base: en, sv. [whisper] extra_languages = added codes. Everywhere (dictation checkboxes, meeting/file language lists, tray, prompt) offers base + added; meetings also get 'Mixed: your languages' (detected per piece) + Detect. Dictation model: large-v3 when any chosen language isn't one turbo handles well (sv, el and lower-resource ones). Names for any code via a shared table checked against faster-whisper's list. Removing an added language also drops it from the dictation set.
close_reason: Merged to main and shipped in Ecoscribe 1.6.0 (installed on Windows 2026-10-07).

title: Dictation: your languages (any mix of en/es/sv/el), auto-detect among them, language shown on the pill, Right Ctrl+L forces the next one
description: Choose which languages dictation listens for (any mix), auto-detected among them; the pill shows the language it heard; dictation key + L forces the next one.
design: Settings: multi-select languages (en, es, sv, el; any mix, Greek new for dictation), saved without a restart where possible. Auto: detect among only those per dictation; sticky toward the last language when the call is close. Model: sv or el in the set -> large-v3 (int8_float16), else turbo. Pill: '✓ ES' briefly after the paste when >1 language. Override: hold the dictation key + L cycles the NEXT dictation Auto -> EN -> ES -> SV -> EL -> Auto, pill shows it; L swallowed. Windows in this PR; Mac key = new capability row with a macos ticket.
close_reason: Merged to main and shipped in Ecoscribe 1.6.0 (installed on Windows 2026-10-07).

title: Delete a dictation from History
description: The user wants to delete dictations from History. A Delete button per row (with the hover buttons), a few seconds to Undo, then the line leaves history.jsonl and its kept audio goes too. The background app owns history.jsonl (it appends under a lock), so the delete runs there; with the app not running the window rewrites the file itself.

title: Name a meeting from the Google Meet tab title when there's no calendar link
description: Some company Google accounts hide the secret iCal address, so the calendar can't name meetings. Instant meetings show only a code (abc-defg-hij): those keep the default name. Read-only: the titles are already read for call detection.
acceptance_criteria: A browser Meet call with no calendar event is named after the Meet tab's event name; a code-only title or no Meet tab keeps 'Meeting'; the calendar still wins when it has an event; works with Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Brave suffixes and on macOS titles.

title: Speakers: don't split the other side into more voices than the invite has people
description: A two-person call (the user and one other person) came out as Me, Speaker 1 and Speaker 2: the diarizer split the one remote voice in two. Better: when the meeting's calendar invite lists N other people (meta calendar.attendees), cap the other side's speaker count at N (pyannote max_speakers / num_speakers), and with N = 1 label them by that name directly. Also worth having: a Merge speakers action on the meeting page.
